questions.prompt: What is a loop invariant used for when designing an algorithm?

options.text: To state a property that holds before and after every iteration, proving correctness
To sort an array in place

questions.prompt: Why is starting with a brute-force solution valuable before optimizing?

options.text: Brute force always runs in O(1) space
Go compilers optimize brute force into O(log n)
It validates your understanding of the spec and serves as a reference oracle for testing faster versions

questions.prompt: In Go, what is the standard pattern for testing an algorithm across many edge cases cleanly?

options.text: Table-driven tests looping over a slice of `{name, input, want}` cases with `t.Run`

questions.prompt: Select all essential parts of a well-specified algorithm problem before coding. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The variable names used in the caller
Expected output format and edge-case behavior

questions.prompt: Match each asymptotic notation to its formal meaning.

Asymptotic lower bound (grows at least as fast as f)

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of this nested loop?
What is the time complexity when a loop halves `n` on each step?
In a doubling experiment, doubling `n` causes runtime to jump 4x. What is the likely complexity?
Why is `append` on a Go slice `O(1)` amortized despite occasional `O(n)` reallocations?

options.text: The garbage collector copies slices in background threads
Capacity doubles (or grows geometrically), so copying `n` elements happens after `~n` cheap appends

questions.prompt: Which two ingredients must every terminating recursive function have? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Two recursive calls and a loop
A global counter and a mutex
A recursive step moving toward a base case

questions.prompt: What happens in Go if a recursive function exceeds the maximum goroutine stack size?

options.text: The runtime panics with `runtime: goroutine stack exceeds ...` (stack overflow)
Go automatically converts it to tail-call iteration
It silently returns the zero value
It switches to heap allocation for stack frames

questions.prompt: What does this recursive function compute for `n >= 0`?
What is the time complexity of naive `fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)` without memoization?
How do you convert any DFS-style recursive algorithm into an iterative one?

options.text: Replace the function with a `switch` statement
Simulate the call stack explicitly with a slice/stack of frames

questions.prompt: What three fields make up a Go slice header at runtime?

options.text: Pointer to backing array, length (`len`), and capacity (`cap`)
Hash seed, bucket count, and flags
Type ID, interface pointer, and size

questions.prompt: What does `b` contain after `a[1:3]` and `b[0] = 99` execute?

options.text: `a` is unchanged because slices copy on sub-slicing
`a[1]` also becomes `99` because `a` and `b` share the same backing array

questions.prompt: In Go, what is the effect of the full slice expression `a[1:3:3]`?

options.text: It sets `cap(b) = 3 - 1 = 2` so `append(b, x)` allocates a new array instead of overwriting `a[3]`

questions.prompt: Select all statements that are true about Go's built-in `map[K]V`. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Maps are safe for concurrent writes without synchronization

questions.prompt: Match each Go data structure to its primary performance strength.

columns.label: Contiguous memory, O(1) index access, cache-friendly iteration
O(1) average key lookup and insertion
O(1) splice/remove given an existing `*Element` node

questions.prompt: When is the two-pointer technique most effective on a slice?

options.text: Only when the slice contains strings
When elements are stored in a hash map
When the slice is sorted or symmetric so inward/same-direction pointers eliminate nested scans

questions.prompt: What does a prefix-sum array `pref[i+1] = pref[i] + nums[i]` enable?

options.text: Answering any subarray sum `[l..r]` in O(1) via `pref[r+1] - pref[l]`
Reversing a linked list in place

questions.prompt: What problem pattern is a fixed- or variable-size sliding window best suited for?

options.text: Contiguous subarray or substring problems with monotonic window validity

questions.prompt: Why do linked list implementations often use a dummy sentinel head node?

options.text: To eliminate special-case `head == nil` checks during insertions and deletions at the front

questions.prompt: How does Floyd's tortoise-and-hare algorithm detect a cycle in a linked list in O(1) space?

options.text: By storing visited pointers in a `map`
By advancing `slow` 1 step and `fast` 2 steps until they meet or `fast` hits `nil`

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of reversing a singly linked list iteratively in place?

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) space

questions.prompt: Which rule defines a stack vs a queue?

options.text: Stack is FIFO; Queue is LIFO
Stack is LIFO (last-in, first-out); Queue is FIFO (first-in, first-out)

questions.prompt: Why can a naive Go slice queue `q = q[1:]` leak memory over long-running streams?

options.text: `q[1:]` copies the whole slice on every pop
The backing array keeps references to popped elements and grows without shrinking until reallocated

questions.prompt: What does a ring buffer (circular queue) use to wrap indices in O(1) time?

options.text: Modulo arithmetic `(idx + 1) % cap` (or bitwise `& (cap - 1)` for power-of-2 capacity)

questions.prompt: What is a monotonic stack commonly used to find in O(n) time?

options.text: The next greater (or smaller) element for every item in an array
The shortest path in a weighted graph

options.text: Insert a new node immediately before or after the given node

questions.prompt: What is the space complexity of a recursive function with maximum call depth `d`?
Why is `strings.Builder` preferred over `s += chunk` inside a loop of `n` iterations in Go?

options.text: Strings in Go are immutable, so `s += chunk` copies all prior bytes each iteration (O(n^2) total)

questions.prompt: What does `cap(s)` report for a Go slice `s`?

options.text: The maximum elements `s` can hold from its start index to the end of its backing array before reallocating
The number of elements currently in `s`
The byte size of one element
The total heap memory of the program
